title: Alternating Harmonic Series: $\eta(1) = \ln 2$
content: Defines the alternating harmonic partial sum $\sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^{k-1}/k$ and states that it converges to $\ln 2$. This is the Dirichlet eta function at $s = 1$: $\eta(1) = 1 - 1/2 + 1/3 - 1/4 + \cdots = \ln 2$. It is also the Taylor series of $\ln(1+x)$ at $x = 1$ (conditionally convergent). The series converges by the alternating series test (Leibniz criterion).

title: Catalan's Constant: $G = \beta(2)$
content: Defines Catalan's constant $G = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^n/(2n+1)^2 \approx 0.9159$ as $\beta(2)$, the Dirichlet beta function at $s = 2$. States convergence, positivity ($G > 0$), and an approximate value. Catalan's constant appears in combinatorics (number of $n$-step staircase polygons), statistical mechanics, and evaluation of definite integrals. Its irrationality is one of the major open problems in number theory.

title: The Unifying Framework: $\beta(s)$ and $\eta(s)$
content: Presents the complete table of Leibniz-type formulas: $\beta(1) = \pi/4$ (Leibniz), $\beta(2) = G$ (Catalan), $\beta(3) = \pi^3/32$ (Euler), $\eta(1) = \ln 2$, $\eta(2) = \pi^2/12$. The Dirichlet beta function $\beta(s) = \sum (-1)^n/(2n+1)^s$ captures odd-denominator alternating series, while the Dirichlet eta function $\eta(s) = \sum (-1)^{n-1}/n^s$ captures all-denominator alternating series. The eta-zeta relation $\eta(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$ converts between alternating and non-alternating sums.
mathContext: $\beta(s) = L(s, \chi_4)$ for the non-principal character mod 4; $\eta(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$.

title: Dirichlet Character $\chi_4$ and L-Function Structure
content: Defines the non-principal Dirichlet character modulo 4: $\chi_4(n) = 0$ if $2 \mid n$, $1$ if $n \equiv 1 \pmod{4}$, $-1$ if $n \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$. Proves periodicity ($\chi_4(n+4) = \chi_4(n)$) and multiplicativity. The beta function is then $\beta(s) = L(s, \chi_4) = \sum \chi_4(n)/n^s$, revealing the number-theoretic structure underlying Leibniz's formula.
